blocks.c: She went back at dusk, which is the hour the profession is built around, and she went the long way so she would arrive from the dark end and see the lamp the way the lane saw it.
It was lit. Of course it was lit. She had lit it herself the day before and the oil was good and the housing was sealed, and there was no mystery in a lamp doing exactly what a lamp is for.
The mystery was in the mud, where a fresh set of prints came up the lane towards her, made by boots the size of her own, stopping where she was standing, and going no further.

Ines took the ink pot from her coat. She rolled back her sleeve. Eleven strokes, four of them smudged, and she added a twelfth in the careful, deliberate way you add a thing you intend to be able to point at later.

Above her the wick burned amber and steady and entirely without opinion. Somewhere behind her, at the far end of a round she had not walked yet, another lamp waited to be attended, and the song had a sixth line, and the ledger had a column for all of it.
She picked up the ladder and went to find out what the circles meant.
